title: Operational Lifecycle Simulation Blueprint
author: Ethan Kim
body:
Overview This blueprint defines a repeatable, auditable process for running platform-level operational lifecycle simulations (op-life sims). It standardizes scenario definitions, execution tooling, artifact capture, and acceptance criteria so engineering and operations teams can validate production behaviors without surprise. The document targets platform, runtime, and observability owners. Objectives - Verify autoscaler and capacity behaviors for multi-tenant inference traffic under stress. - Exercise graceful degradation and model-variant fallback paths. - Validate operator runbooks and reduce time-to-recovery through measured practice. - Reveal telemetry gaps and reduce alert noise during realistic failure sequences. Scope and non-goals - In scope: serving runtime, routing policy behaviors, KV/prefix cache integrity, autoscaler interactions, and observability/alerting pipelines. - Out of scope: model training, offline batch pipelines, and billing/reconciliation systems. Roles and ownership - Simulation Owner: eng-platform/gameday (primary). - Scenario Lead: rotating senior platform engineer (assign per run). - Observability Lead: eng-platform/dashboards (responsible for SLI dashboards and artifact exports). - Incident Facilitator: on-call platform operator (executes runbook during the sim). - Postmortem Owner: Simulation Owner (publishes findings and action items). Simulation catalog (high-level types) 1) Capacity Saturation (steady & burst): tests autoscaler hysteresis, queue behavior, and eviction patterns. 2) KV/Prefix Cache Loss: validates cache rehydration, increased cold-hit latencies, and correctness of prefix cache fallback. 3) Model-Variant Cascade: induces errors in a primary model variant to verify automatic swap to quantized/cheaper variants and correctness scoring. 4) Regional Degradation / Blackhole: simulates regional network egress failures and validates cross-region failover routing and safety limits. 5) Alert-Noise Storm: intentionally creates large volumes of low-priority alerts to validate notification throttles and operator prioritization. 6) Cold-Start Wave: mass cold-starts across GPU pools to exercise warmup logic and in-flight request shaping. Cadence and schedule - Quarterly: full-suite run across all scenarios; planning week + 2-day execution window. - Monthly: focused run (1-2 scenarios); 1 day planning + 4-hour execution window. - Pre-release: gated ad-hoc run 48-72 hours before major rollouts that touch routing/autoscaling. Pre-sim checklist (operator preflight) - Create a dedicated simulation namespace: label with sim=true and reserve resource quotas. - Enable telemetry snapshot retention and ensure trace sampling is increased for the sim window. - Notify stakeholders (#platform-gameday, #sre-notices) and schedule a pre-sim briefing. - Confirm runbooks, rollback artifacts, and operator contact rotations are visible in the runbook binder. Execution playbook (short form) 1) Provision synthetic tenant cohort and boot workload generators that mirror the top-ten customer profiles. 2) Collect a 30-minute baseline of traces, SLIs, and critical metrics. 3) Run the scenario-specific failure script (see below). 4) Operators follow the runbook; automated remediations may be toggled after an initial manual verification window (default: 30 minutes). 5) Record operator actions, timestamps, Slack/hand-off messages, and time-to-restoration relative to SLOs. 6) Rehydrate services and execute post-restore validation (golden prompt checks for model-variant tests). Scenario scripts (examples, stepwise) - Capacity Saturation (steady then burst): 1) Ramp synthetic RPS by +350% over 15 minutes using the P95 sequence length distribution. 2) After 30 minutes, perform three 2-minute bursts at 3x the current load with 5-minute rests. 3) Observe autoscaler scale events, preemptible evictions, queue depth, and per-tenant throttling. - KV/Prefix Cache Failover: 1) Drain KV shard instances in one availability zone (e.g., us-east-1a) for 10 minutes. 2) Increase request KV-miss ratio by 20% and monitor latency and rehydration time. 3) Validate cache rehydration metrics and fairness logs for tenant impact. - Model-Variant Cascade: 1) Induce a controlled error condition in the primary model variant (synthetic corrupt weights or throttled inference path). 2) Trigger automatic fallback to the quantized or cheaper variant. 3) Run golden-set correctness checks and compare semantic-similarity and hallucination rates to baseline. Environment configuration matrix (reference) - GPU pool (regional): minimum 16 nodes (A100/80GB equiv). Simulation knobs: add_preemptible = true; drain_percentage = 30%. - Autoscaler: target_utilization = 0.75; scale_step = 8; cooldown = 120s. - KV shards: 64 shards; fail_fraction = 0.25; rehydration_backoff = 30s. - Routing policy: cost-first fallback allowed; prefer_local = false; max_failover_hops = 2. SLIs and acceptance criteria - Latency SLI: P95 generation latency < 500ms for tier-1 tenants during steady-state. During controlled degradation, fallback target P95 < 1200ms. - Availability SLI: successful request rate >= 99.0% for tier-1 during simulation; >= 95% for tier-2. - Correctness SLI (model-variant fallback): batch semantic-similarity score >= 0.88 vs golden set (tooling: eval-harness). - Operator reaction: pager acknowledgment < 5 minutes for P1 signals. Observability and artifact capture - Dashboard snapshots: export JSON for the canonical dashboards associated with the simulation. - Traces: sample 500 representative traces covering baseline, failure injection, and recovery windows. - Logs: aggregate logs for the sim namespace and include correlated trace IDs. - Metric dump: export raw series with 1s granularity for the sim window for: token_throughput, kv_miss_rate, model_variant_swap_count, autoscaler_events. Failure injection primitives (CLI examples) - otc-sim-kill-service --service --region --duration - otc-sim-drop-egress --region --percent

- otc-sim-increase-rps --tenant --factor - otc-sim-drain-kv-shards --shard-set --fraction Operator snippets (common) - Create simulation namespace: export SIM_NS=platform-sim-$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M) kubectl create ns $SIM_NS --labels=sim=true - Start synthetic traffic (example): sim-traffic --namespace $SIM_NS --profile top10-profiles.yaml --rps 5000 --duration 2h - Safe service kill: otc-sim-kill-service --service runtime-gpu-pool --region us-east-1 --duration 120 Post-run analysis template (for the retro) - Collected artifacts: dashboards (JSON), trace bundle, raw metric dump, aggregated logs, operator action timeline. - Retro questions (timestamped evidence required): 1) Which SLIs were breached and what sequence of events led to the breach? 2) Did runbook guidance lead operators to correct remediation steps? Highlight ambiguous instructions. 3) Were automated remediations beneficial or harmful? Provide examples and metrics. 4) What telemetry gaps or blind spots were discovered? 5) Action items (owner, ETA, priority). Retrospective cadence and artifacts - A blameless postmortem (60-90 minutes) must be scheduled within 3 business days. - Publish a 1-2 page findings memo and tag any runbook changes in the runbook repo. - Capture all action items in the platform backlog and assign severity tags (critical/high/medium/low). Automation roadmap (3 quarters) - Q1: Sim-as-code library: scenario templates and a single CLI to run full-suite sims with automated artifact collection. - Q2: Integrate golden-sample correctness checks into the sim pipeline and produce automatic scoring reports. - Q3: Runbook autopilot: implement gated automation for low-risk remediations (routing shift, circuit open) with operator approval flows. Risks and mitigations - Risk: Cross-contamination of production capacity (shared Dedicated pools). Mitigation: Mandatory namespace isolation and enforce resource reservations and soft quotas. - Risk: Alert fatigue from frequent runs. Mitigation: Use dedicated notification channels, tag sim-origin alerts (sim=true), and temporarily suppress non-actionable noise. Related pages and references - /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/platform-gameday-exercise-automation-and-scripting-playbook-2026 - /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/llm-quality-regression-alerting-and-dashboard-guidelines-2026 Appendix: example synthetic workload config (YAML) # top10-profiles.yaml profiles: - name: chat-short rps_ratio: 0.45 seq_len_p95: 64 prompt_variability: medium - name: completion-long rps_ratio: 0.35 seq_len_p95: 512 prompt_variability: low - name: rerank-burst rps_ratio: 0.2 seq_len_p95: 128 burstiness: true End of document
